moments.selftext: Before Robert Pattinson became one of Hollywood’s biggest stars, he admitted to inventing a far more prestigious background for himself. He claimed he had studied at Oxford and trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, even telling people in Los Angeles that Prince William had attended RADA with him. The stories were completely fabricated. Pattinson later admitted that he assumed Americans would believe almost anything an English actor told them if it sounded prestigious enough. He also became surprisingly open in interviews about his habit of making up stories.

moments.selftext: In November 2016, a massive sinkhole suddenly opened in central Fukuoka following nearby subway construction. The collapse stretched roughly 30 meters (98 feet) across and 15 meters (49 feet) deep. Crews worked around the clock, filling the crater with thousands of cubic meters of material and restoring damaged underground utilities. After extensive safety testing, the road reopened to traffic in about a week, although monitoring and permanent repairs continued afterward. Japan is known for its exceptionally well-maintained roads, with potholes relatively rare even in crowded cities like Tokyo and Osaka. Instead of waiting for damage to worsen, municipalities regularly inspect roads, carry out preventative maintenance, and repair problems quickly—often within days.

moments.title: Record highs are back. What comes next? The S&P 500 has risen in 13 of the last 17 instances following a significant breakout to an all-time high over the last 30 years. During these periods, the index gained an average
moments.selftext: Record highs are back. What comes next? The S&P 500 has risen in 13 of the last 17 instances following a significant breakout to an all-time high over the last 30 years. During these periods, the index gained an average of ~6.3% over the subsequent 6 months. The 4 exceptions came in 2000, 2007, 2018, and 2019, with the first two preceding major bear markets. Most recently, in 2025, the S&P 500 gained +12.3% in the 6 months following a similar move to an all-time high. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted 26 all-time highs in 2026, following 39 record closes in full-year 2025 and 57 in 2024. History suggests market momentum is set to continue.
